title: The merge prose judge gets a readable verdict, or says why not
why: On mailaudit #222, the merge-time prose judge returned UNKNOWN on both lines with "no readable verdict" (runner 9, 23:08 CST Nov 7).
note: No step owned verdict parsing (triage searched, 23:12 CST). First find the cause: the model reply, the parser or the excerpt. Related: steps prose-judge-exception-count (lines not judged after an exception) and judge-sees-named-code. Slug and title by triage; no source gave one. Waits under the item 384 hold unless the coordinator counts it as a queue fix. Not a queue fix: mailaudit #222 merged at 23:08 CST with the UNKNOWN lines, so it blocked nothing. Held (coordinator, 23:10 CST). Repeats (runner 9, [ended:batch-runner-9-(child-repos)]): q_max merge #1125 (02:40 CST Nov 8) had 1 line with "no readable verdict", and #1129 (03:28 CST) had 2; each unread line passed unjudged. Now a queue fix (coordinator, 03:27 CST Nov 8; it suggested the slug prose-judge-no-verdict, folded in here). Fix: find why the judge's answer does not parse, and have each unread line name itself as UNKNOWN in the merge output. Red case first: a judge reply the parser cannot read gives a line that passes with no mention today. Lane [ended:lane:-judge-no-readable-verdict] started it (coordinator, 03:27 CST Nov 8).
